Stealth Mode
Hide user-installed apps on Android car head units before service visits.

Author
Dezz — Telegram @DezzK

Source code
github.com/DezzK/stealth

If the app does not come back after dialing the PIN
Some head-unit dialers do not report outgoing calls to apps. Connect a computer and run:
adb shell am start -n dezz.stealth/.MainActivity
or, to bring the launcher icon back:
adb shell pm enable dezz.stealth/.LauncherTrampolineActivity

The full About page is available online at dezzk.github.io/stealth when an internet connection is available.

A PIN code is required before hiding apps. After hiding, the app icon will disappear. To reveal it again, open the dialer, enter your PIN, and press the call button.\n\nSet a numeric PIN (minimum 3 digits):
Phone call permissions are required for the PIN unlock feature. Without them, you won\'t be able to reveal the app by dialing your PIN.

To hide apps, the application needs phone call permissions. Without them, after hiding you will not be able to reveal the app by dialing PIN — the app icon will remain hidden with no way to restore it.\n\nGrant the permissions?

Phone call permissions were previously denied. To grant them, go to the app settings and enable them manually. Without these permissions, after hiding you will not be able to reveal the app by dialing PIN.

After a few days the head unit may unload the app from memory, and then dialing the PIN won\'t reveal it. Letting the app ignore battery optimization makes this much less likely.\n\nOpen the system dialog to allow it?
